summary: Intermittent p99 latency bursts due to KV-cache coordination and request stitching in continuous-batcher
description:
Issue summary: Customers (notably TextFlow.ai dedicated cluster) report intermittent p99 spikes and occasional 504 timeouts originating from the continuous batching path. Spikes appear as short-lived bursts (30s-3m) and correlate with small increases in concurrent KV-cache coordination activity and request stitching events.

Impact: Elevated tail latency (p99) for text generation requests causing timeouts for a subset of customer requests. Customer workloads are latency-sensitive (chat/LLM UX) and observe degraded user experience during bursts.

Environment: Dedicated deployment for TextFlow.ai in us-east-1, running Serving Runtime v2.9.1 with continuous-batcher enabled, KV-cache version 1.4.0. Autoscaling configured with min 2, max 8 GPUs.

Observed: Sudden p99 jumps from baseline ~300ms to 2.5s+ with some 504s when concurrent stitching and KV-cache invalidation overlap. Metrics show increased syscall wait and per-batch serialization time during the window.

Expected: Stable p95/p99 within SLO (p95 < 500ms, p99 < 1s) and graceful handling of KV-cache refresh and request coalescing without per-request stalls.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a steady low-QPS mix of short and medium prompts that exercise streaming and non-streaming paths. 2) Trigger KV-cache refresh by rolling a small model variant (or by simulated cache invalidation). 3) At the same time inject a small burst of short concurrent requests (20-40 qps for 30s). 4) Observe p99 on the dedicated cluster and check serving-runtime /batcher logs during the timeframe.
observed_behavior: p99 jumps and intermittent 504s during overlapping KV-cache invalidation and request-stitching windows. Continuous-batcher shows several consecutive 'flush' cycles where one microbatch holds execution until a stitched sub-batch completes causing head-of-line delays.
expected_behavior: Continuous-batcher should avoid head-of-line stalls when KV-cache coordination occurs; stitched requests should proceed without blocking unrelated microbatches and timeouts should be rare.

sample logs (timestamps redacted):

[2026-03-10T15:03:12Z] kv-cache: invalidation queued keys=37
[2026-03-10T15:03:12Z] batcher: stitch_waiting count=5 wait_reason=kv-coord
[2026-03-10T15:03:13Z] serving-runtime: serialization_lock acquired duration=128ms
[2026-03-10T15:03:15Z] batcher: flush delayed delay=934ms cause=stitch-block
[2026-03-10T15:03:16Z] gateway: response_timeout code=504 route=/v1/generate
[2026-03-10T15:04:10Z] metrics: p99=2536ms p95=612ms
investigation_notes:
- Correlated customer p99 spikes with short bursts of KV-cache invalidation created by model rollout automation.
- Traced batcher logs: several microbatches transitioned to 'await_stitch' due to pending KV-coordination RPCs; while waiting they held serialization locks that prevented other microbatches from proceeding in the same worker.
- Kernel-level traces show increased futex/syswait around the timeouts; likely contention on per-worker serialization.
- Reproduced locally in a staging dedicated cluster by forcing KV-cache refresh + short request burst; observed same head-of-line behavior.
- Differences vs prior incidents: previously observed linger/timer drift; here root cause appears to be combination of KV-cache RPCs taken synchronously inside the batcher critical path and the stitch aggregation logic not yielding to unrelated microbatches.
hypothesis: Synchronous KV-cache coordination calls injected into the continuous-batcher critical section cause per-worker serialization waits. When request-stitching aggregates sub-requests waiting on KV replies, a microbatch can block the worker thread and create head-of-line blocking across other microbatches, resulting in transient p99 spikes and 504s.
mitigation_workaround: 1) Recommend immediate mitigation for TextFlow.ai: disable KV-cache synchronous refresh during peak windows (toggle to async refresh) and temporarily reduce model rollout frequency. 2) Increase dedicated pool to add more worker capacity (short-term relief). 3) If acceptable, disable request stitching for the tenant via tenant-config to avoid aggregated stitch wait (note: cost/efficiency tradeoff).
next_steps:
1) Engineering: instrument batcher to measure time spent in KV-coord critical section and count blocked microbatches. 2) Create a runtime change to make KV-cache RPCs asynchronous or move them outside the batcher serialization lock. 3) Add backpressure/timeout on stitch wait so microbatches can proceed if sub-requests exceed X ms. 4) Schedule a rollout of the patch to staging and run controlled chaos to verify. 5) Communicate workaround to customer and update runbook.
Owners: Jonah Kim (runtime), Priya Gupta (kv-cache).
resolution: Triaging - workaround communicated to customer; engineering investigation in progress. Patch planned to decouple KV-cache calls from batcher critical path.
